Ana — thanks, and good questions. High level: we try to reflect credit notes against the outstanding USD invoice amount in our accounting system before any FX conversion we do for internal reconciliation. That said, bank-side intermediary deductions are external to that ledger flow and typically reduce the net amount posted to our beneficiary account.

Practical approach we recommend:
- Please instruct your remitter to select "OUR" (beneficiary pays all intermediaries) if Globex can accept paying correspondent fees; this preserves gross-settlement amounts on our end. If you must use "BEN" (beneficiary-charges), the net shortfall will be visible and the credit application may not fully cover the gap after FX.
- Include this exact reference on the wire: GLX-INV-7891 / CRN-600 followed by the SWIFT trace (e.g., 20270519GBXL12345). Put that string in the Payment Details and Remittance Reference fields.
- Send the credit-note PDF to billing@redwood.ai (we received the stub but ask that it be uploaded to the HubSpot deal thread).

I'm looping Marissa to confirm the ledger FX handling and Ben for treasury on the correspondent chain trace.

Best,
Rachel

Hi all — quick follow-up with specifics from ops/treasury: 

1) Ledger treatment: We post invoices in USD (customer is billed in USD). When we receive an EUR remittance, treasury books the incoming EUR and runs an internal FX conversion for reconciliation. The credit note (EUR 600) will be recorded against the invoice before we close the statement, but the timing matters — if the bank chain already deducted intermediaries before funds landed, the net credit available for application may be lower.

2) Intermediary fees: Two common patterns we see:
- Sender-paid (OUR): Gross amount arrives and our systems reconcile to the invoice total; any FX is internal and transparent. This is preferred for clean matching.
- Receiver-paid (BEN/SHA): The bank chain removes fees en route; the amount posted is net. In that case we record the net as received and will mark the invoice partially paid; the credit note will be applied against the outstanding balance after netting. If the net shortfall remains, we will raise the shortfall to the customer for collection or apply the credit note proportionally.

3) Trace/format: Please include the following exact fields on the payment instruction to help treasury: 
   - Remittance reference: GLX-INV-7891 / CRN-600
   - Originator -> Ordered By: Globex Payments (Globex Holdings S.A.)
   - Beneficiary bank FBO: Redwood Inference Ltd — acct sample below (also attached as our_nostro_account_sample.pdf)
   - SWIFT Trace: include any MT103/202 reference in the payment details field; if you have a fixed MT199/ack use that too.

4) If intermediaries are unknown, include the intermediary-bank name and any correspondent BICs you were given. If possible ask your bank to process as OUR. If they cannot, we suggest instructing them to add an additional remittance message: "Apply CRN-600 before currency conversion" so that accounting has explicit direction.

Attachment: INV-7891-credit-note.pdf (we will place copy on the HubSpot deal).

Ben — note the remittance string above and confirm whether treasury can reconstitute the FX impact and whether Redwood will absorb any rounding variance under $5 in USD equivalent (we can make a one-off concession for large enterprise on first settlement).

Thanks,
Marissa
Head of Revenue Operations — Redwood Inference
